about: Proven drink structures the generator builds from (see web/lib/composer.js). Compiled from research by scripts/archetypes-build.mjs.

archetypes.name: Zombie
archetypes.definition: A tall, deceptively smooth flash-blended punch of three contrasting rums (light/gold column, funky Jamaican, and an overproof Demerara kicker) balanced by lime and grapefruit, sweetened and spiced by falernum, cinnamon (Don's Mix) and a little grenadine, and seasoned with drops of anise and Angostura.

signature.note: At least two distinct styles: a clean column-still gold/light rum plus a Jamaican (or other pot-still) rum for funk. Counts excluding the overproof.
151 Demerara is canonical (Lemon Hart / Hamilton). It is mixed in, never floated, in the Don original; the burning 151 float is a later chain-restaurant habit.
Either 1/2 oz Don's Mix or 1/4 oz white grapefruit + 1/4 oz cinnamon syrup. The c. 1950 Don version swaps this for pineapple + passion fruit; allowed only via the passion-fruit route below.
One teaspoon. It is there for depth, not color; it must not turn the drink red.
6 drops (about 1/8 tsp) Pernod or Herbsaint; Smuggler's Cove uses Herbstura (Herbsaint + Angostura 1:1).
1-2 dashes.

optional.note: Don's c. 1950 Zombie replaced Don's Mix and falernum with passion fruit syrup, pineapple, lemon and a teaspoon of brown sugar. Use as a set, not piecemeal.

canonicalSpecs.name: Zombie (1934)
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, Hollywood, 1934; decoded by Jeff Berry from bartender Dick Santiago's 1937 notebook (Sippin' Safari, 2007; Beachbum Berry Remixed, 2010)

lines.orig: Don's Mix: 2 parts white grapefruit : 1 part cinnamon syrup

canonicalSpecs.note: Flash-blend with 6 oz crushed ice no more than 5 seconds; pour into a chimney glass and top with ice cubes to fill. Don limited guests to two.

canonicalSpecs.name: Zombie (Don the Beachcomber, c. 1950)
canonicalSpecs.source: Don's later Zombie as printed by Louis Spievak (1950); reprinted in Berry, Intoxica! (2002)

lines.orig: 1 tsp brown sugar dissolved in the citrus

canonicalSpecs.note: Shows that Don himself changed the formula; this is the line the mid-century bar guides (and their apricot-brandy Zombies) descend from.

canonicalSpecs.name: Zombie (Smuggler's Cove)
canonicalSpecs.source: Martin & Rebecca Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016); also Punch

lines.orig: black blended overproof rum (Hamilton / Lemon Hart 151)

canonicalSpecs.note: Flash-blend with 12 oz crushed ice; pour into a chimney/collins glass.

canonicalSpecs.name: Trader Vic's Zombie (1946)
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Book of Food and Drink (1946), pp. 70-71
canonicalSpecs.note: Vic's own answer to Don's drink: curaçao and orange instead of falernum and Don's Mix. Useful as proof that a Zombie is defined by the rum stack and strength, not one fixed syrup.

ratios.notes: baseOz includes the 3/4-1 oz overproof. A Zombie is the tartest, strongest family in the catalogue (model: ~19% ABV for the 1934 spec before the extra cubes it is topped with; real-world ~15-17%). Do not exceed ~4 oz total rum or ~1 oz of 151. sourOz 2.0 only in the c. 1950 lime + lemon version.

never: orange wheel fan as the only garnish

archetypes.look: Tall chimney glass packed with crushed ice and topped with cubes; the liquid reads deep amber to burnished copper (from Jamaican and 151 Demerara rum), lightly hazy from grapefruit and lime, with at most a faint rosy cast from the single teaspoon of grenadine. Not red, not orange-juice orange, not layered. A tall mint sprig rises from the top. The c. 1950 passion-fruit version is a paler, cloudier golden-orange.
substitutions: Smith & Cross or Appleton 12 for the gold/dark Jamaican rum
Hamilton 151 or Plantation (Planteray) OFTD for Lemon Hart 151
1/4 oz white grapefruit + 1/4 oz cinnamon syrup for 1/2 oz Don's Mix
Herbsaint, absinthe or Pernod interchangeably for the anise drops
falernum syrup for Velvet Falernum (drink gets slightly less strong, slightly sweeter)
aged Barbados or column-aged rum for the gold Puerto Rican rum
redFlags: a bright red drink (grenadine by the ounce)
pineapple + orange juice + apricot brandy "Zombie" (1960s bar-guide debasement) presented as the original
served short or in a coupe
more than ~4 oz total rum (dangerous, not just strong)
flaming 151 float presented as authentic Don
orange juice as the main juice
anise in ounces rather than drops

archetypes.name: Test Pilot / Jet Pilot
archetypes.definition: A short, rum-heavy Beachcomber sour in a double old fashioned: dark Jamaican-led rums with lime, falernum and either Cointreau (Test Pilot) or grapefruit-cinnamon (Jet Pilot), seasoned with Pernod and Angostura and flash-blended.
classics: Jet Pilot (The Luau, Beverly Hills, c. 1958)

signature.note: Only half an ounce: the Pilots are drier and more spirit-forward than the Zombie.
Test Pilot: 1/2 oz Cointreau. Jet Pilot: 1/2 oz grapefruit + 1/2 oz cinnamon syrup.
6 drops Pernod + 1 dash Angostura.

optional.note: Required for a Jet Pilot, absent from the Test Pilot.

canonicalSpecs.name: Test Pilot
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, c. 1941; Jeff Berry, Grog Log (1998) / Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend with 1 cup crushed ice for 5 seconds; pour unstrained.

canonicalSpecs.name: Jet Pilot
canonicalSpecs.source: The Luau, Beverly Hills (Steve Crane), c. 1958; Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007) p. 130; same in Smuggler's Cove (2016)
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend with 4 oz crushed ice for 5 seconds.

canonicalSpecs.name: Jet Pilot (Smuggler's Cove)
canonicalSpecs.source: Martin & Rebecca Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016)

ratios.notes: Short and strong; only 1/2 oz lime. Test Pilot has no overproof (2.25 oz rum); Jet Pilot adds 3/4 oz 151 inside its 2.5 oz rum.

archetypes.look: Double old fashioned of crushed ice holding a translucent, deep amber-brown liquid (dark Jamaican rum dominates); the Test Pilot is nearly clear amber with a slight lime haze, the Jet Pilot a touch cloudier and more copper from grapefruit. No layers, no foam.
substitutions: Coruba or Hamilton Jamaican Pot Still Black for dark Jamaican
dry curaçao for Cointreau in the Test Pilot
Hamilton 151 or OFTD for Lemon Hart 151
Herbstura for separate Pernod + Angostura
redFlags: served tall or in a hurricane
sweet and soft rather than strong and dry

archetypes.name: Cobra's Fang
archetypes.definition: A short, fierce overproof-Demerara drink: 151 rum as nearly the whole base, cut with lime and orange and sweetened with red fruit syrup (fassionola) and falernum, seasoned with absinthe and Angostura.

signature.note: The overproof IS the base here, not a kicker.
Half and half.
Fassionola (red passion-fruit/berry syrup) is the historical ingredient; the vocabulary has no id for it (see missingIngredients). Plain passion fruit syrup is the accepted stand-in.

optional.note: Modern specs (Death & Co) soften the 151 with aged Jamaican.

canonicalSpecs.name: Cobra's Fang
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, c. 1937; Jeff Berry, Grog Log (1998) / Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010) / Total Tiki
canonicalSpecs.note: Flash-blend and pour into a tall glass or Cobra/tiki mug; add ice to fill.

canonicalSpecs.name: Cobra's Fang (Death & Co)
canonicalSpecs.source: Death & Co: Modern Classic Cocktails (2014)

canonicalSpecs.name: Kon-Tiki Cobra
canonicalSpecs.source: Kon-Tiki, Chicago; Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)

ratios.notes: Small volume, high proof because the base is 151. Orange (0.5 oz) is not counted in sourOz.

archetypes.look: With true fassionola: a translucent ruby-orange to garnet over crushed ice (the red syrup over dark 151). With plain passion fruit syrup: a cloudy burnished copper-orange. Mostly seen through a mug; no layers.
substitutions: Hamilton 151 or OFTD for Lemon Hart 151
passion fruit syrup + a barspoon of grenadine or hibiscus syrup for fassionola
Herbsaint or Pernod for absinthe

archetypes.name: Beachcomber Spice Sour
archetypes.definition: A Don-style sour of about two ounces of rum with half-ounce lime and half-ounce orange, sweetened by honey or a spice syrup and perfumed with one of Don's spice modifiers (allspice dram, Don's Spices #2, cinnamon, falernum) plus Angostura; flash-blended and served tall in a pilsner.
classics: Three Dots and a Dash (Don the Beachcomber, WWII)

signature.note: Three Dots: 1 1/2 aged Martinique + 1/2 Demerara. Nui Nui: 2 oz amber Virgin Islands rum.
Equal to the lime: the signature half-and-half citrus of these drinks.
At least two of these, each 1/4 oz.
1 dash.

optional.note: Three Dots uses honey mix; it rounds the allspice.
Some modern Nui Nui specs add 1/4 oz cane syrup.

canonicalSpecs.name: Three Dots and a Dash
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, early 1940s (WWII); Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007); same in Smuggler's Cove (2016)
garnish: 3 cherries and a pineapple chunk on a pick (Morse code 'V': dot-dot-dot-dash)
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend with 6 oz crushed ice for 5 seconds; pour into a tulip/pilsner and add crushed ice to fill.

canonicalSpecs.name: Nui Nui
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, 1930s; Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)

lines.orig: Don's Spices #4 (Berry's reading: cinnamon syrup) - uncertain

canonicalSpecs.name: Nui Nui (Easy Tiki)
canonicalSpecs.source: Brian Miller in Punch, Easy Tiki (2021)

canonicalSpecs.name: Kon-Tiki Mai Tai
canonicalSpecs.source: Kon-Tiki, Cleveland (a Don-style drink, unrelated to Vic's); Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)

ratios.notes: Half-ounce lime + half-ounce orange (orange not counted in sourOz). Spice liqueurs (allspice dram, falernum, Don's Spices #2) count as sweet; keep total sweet <= 1 oz.

archetypes.look: Tall footed pilsner of crushed ice; a hazy golden-amber to soft orange-amber liquid (orange juice + aged rum + honey), lightly opaque, no layers. The Nui Nui reads a little paler gold with a long orange spiral coiled inside the glass.
substitutions: Clément VSOP / Rhum J.M. VSOP for aged Martinique
El Dorado 5 or 8 for Demerara
equal parts vanilla syrup + allspice dram for Don's Spices #2
allspice dram + a little Angostura if falernum is missing (less ideal)
honey syrup for cane syrup
redFlags: pineapple juice as a main component
too sweet (more than ~1 1/4 oz total sweet)
served short in a coupe without ice

archetypes.name: Pearl Diver (Gardenia Punch)
archetypes.definition: Don's iced hot buttered rum: three rums with lime and orange, emulsified with Gardenia Mix (butter, honey, cinnamon, vanilla, allspice) by a hard blend and strained into the Pearl Diver glass.
classics: Pearl Diver / Pearl Diver's Punch (Don the Beachcomber, 1937)

signature.note: Butter-honey-spice batter, kept at room temperature or it will not emulsify.
Gold Puerto Rican lead + Demerara + a little Jamaican.

canonicalSpecs.name: Pearl Diver
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, 1937; Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007); as published by Punch / Smuggler's Cove (2016)

lines.orig: Gardenia Mix: butter, honey, cinnamon syrup, vanilla syrup, allspice dram

canonicalSpecs.note: Gardenia Mix first, ice last; blend at high speed ~15 seconds, strain through a medium sieve into a Pearl Diver glass (fill with crushed ice).

canonicalSpecs.name: Pearl Diver (Easy Tiki)
canonicalSpecs.source: Gaby Mlynarczyk (Accomplice Bar) in Punch, Easy Tiki (2021)

ratios.notes: Gardenia Mix counted as the sweetener (its butter adds body the chemistry model does not see). The Easy Tiki riff (sugar:acid ~25) is a sweeter modern take and excluded from the target.

archetypes.look: A creamy, opaque pale butterscotch-gold drink with a velvety, fine-bubbled top from the emulsified butter; served in the flared, tall Pearl Diver glass (ridged-bottom pilsner). Looks almost like an orange cream soda; no layers.
substitutions: a simplified Gardenia (butter + honey + cinnamon syrup + vanilla syrup + allspice dram) is the only acceptable stand-in; no butterscotch schnapps
El Dorado 5 for Demerara
Appleton Signature for gold Jamaican
redFlags: made without butter (just honey) yet called a Pearl Diver
refrigerated Gardenia that leaves greasy flecks
shaken with cubes instead of blended (butter will not emulsify)

archetypes.name: Port au Prince
archetypes.definition: A gentle Haitian-rum sour with lime, a little pineapple, falernum, a touch of sugar and a whisper of grenadine and Angostura: Don's showcase for Barbancourt.
classics: Port au Prince (Don the Beachcomber, late 1930s)

signature.note: Half an ounce: an accent, not a juice base.
Drops/dash of grenadine, dash of bitters.

canonicalSpecs.name: Port au Prince
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber; Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007) (via SBoudrias transcription)

canonicalSpecs.name: Port au Prince (Smuggler's Cove)
canonicalSpecs.source: Martin & Rebecca Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016); Difford's Guide
garnish: lime wedge with a cocktail umbrella

canonicalSpecs.name: Port au Prince (Death & Co)
canonicalSpecs.source: Death & Co: Modern Classic Cocktails (2014)

ratios.notes: Gentle, short. Pineapple 1/2 oz is an accent counted in totalOz only.

archetypes.look: Pale golden-amber, softly hazy from the pineapple, with a faint blush from the grenadine drops; served over crushed ice in a footed pilsner. Light and bright, not red.
substitutions: Barbancourt 8 for Barbancourt 5 Star
an aged agricole for Haitian rum
falernum syrup for Velvet Falernum

archetypes.name: Beachcomber's Gold (Ice-Shell Daiquiri)
archetypes.definition: A small, elegant Don-style daiquiri of three rums with lime and sugar, scented with drops of Pernod and almond, served in a champagne saucer lined with a molded shell of shaved ice.

signature.note: 6 drops Pernod + 4 drops almond extract.

canonicalSpecs.name: Beachcomber's Gold
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, Hollywood & Palm Springs, 1937; Jeff Berry, Grog Log / Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend briefly, strain into a champagne saucer lined with a frozen shaved-ice shell.

canonicalSpecs.name: Beachcomber's Gold (rum-and-vermouth version)
canonicalSpecs.source: Later printed version (commonly reproduced; low confidence, one of the three versions Berry notes in Remixed)

ratios.notes: A 1:1 lime:syrup daiquiri on 2 oz rum. The vermouth version (low confidence) is excluded from the target.

archetypes.look: A champagne saucer lined with a white, frosted shell of shaved ice; a small pour of translucent pale-gold to light amber liquid sits in the hollow. Jewel-like, clean, no haze beyond lime.
substitutions: orgeat for almond extract only if reducing the sugar
Herbsaint for Pernod
Appleton Signature for gold Jamaican
redFlags: served on rocks in a tumbler

archetypes.name: Missionary's Downfall
archetypes.definition: A frozen daiquiri of light rum, lime, honey and peach brandy blended hard with fresh pineapple and a fistful of mint into a pale-green slush.

signature.note: Apricot is an accepted modern swap.
Ideally 1/4 cup diced fresh pineapple, blended.
About 1/4 cup packed leaves (10-20 leaves); this is the drink's color and identity.

canonicalSpecs.name: Missionary's Downfall
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, 1940s; Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend with 1 cup crushed ice for about 20 seconds; pour into a coupe/cocktail glass.

canonicalSpecs.name: Missionary's Downfall (Easy Tiki)
canonicalSpecs.source: Scotty Schuder (Dirty Dick, Paris) in Punch, Easy Tiki (2021)

canonicalSpecs.name: Shaken Missionary's Downfall
canonicalSpecs.source: Punch, Easy Tiki (2021)

ratios.notes: Frozen drinks need more sugar because cold blunts sweetness; Berry's blended original models at ~23:1 and ~6% ABV (ice becomes drink). The shaken modern version sits ~11:1 and ~13%.

archetypes.look: An opaque, frosty pastel jade/celadon-green slush flecked with darker mint, mounded in a coupe; pineapple warms it toward pale green-gold. Matte, granular, no layers.
substitutions: apricot liqueur for peach brandy
canned unsweetened pineapple juice for fresh chunks (less body)
lemon for lime (Schuder)
redFlags: not green (no mint or mint only as garnish)

archetypes.name: Navy Grog
archetypes.definition: Three ounces of three different rums with equal lime and white grapefruit, sweetened with honey (Don) or demerara and allspice dram (Vic), served over an ice cone with a straw through it.

signature.note: Light + dark Jamaican + Demerara is the classic triad.
White, not pink.
Don: 1 oz honey mix. Vic: 1/4 oz demerara + 1/4 oz allspice dram.

canonicalSpecs.name: Navy Grog (Don the Beachcomber)
canonicalSpecs.source: Don the Beachcomber, c. 1941; Jeff Berry (Grog Log 1998; Beachbum Berry Remixed 2010); Wikipedia

lines.orig: white Cuban / light Puerto Rican rum

garnish: ice cone with a straw through it
canonicalSpecs.note: Shake with ice and pour into a double old fashioned around a shaved-ice cone (packed in a pilsner, bored with a chopstick for the straw, frozen overnight).

canonicalSpecs.name: Navy Grog (Trader Vic's)
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's, 1940s; per Smuggler's Cove / Wikipedia

canonicalSpecs.name: Navy Grog (Tropical Standard)
canonicalSpecs.source: Garret Richard & Ben Schaffer, Tropical Standard (2023)

ratios.notes: Equal lime and white grapefruit; Don's honey version is the rounder (10:1), Vic's demerara + allspice version the drier (5.5:1).

required: straw through an ice cone (or crushed ice)

archetypes.look: A tall white cylinder of frozen shaved ice (the cone) standing in a double old fashioned with a straw down its center; around it a cloudy amber-tan liquid (honey + grapefruit + dark rums), a few fine bubbles from the soda. No layers.
substitutions: Hamilton 86 or El Dorado 5/8 for Demerara
Coruba or Hamilton Pot Still Black for dark Jamaican
Barbancourt white or Flor de Caña 4 for light rum
crushed ice if no cone
redFlags: navy-strength Pusser's alone called a Navy Grog

archetypes.name: Mai Tai
archetypes.definition: Two ounces of characterful aged rum (originally 17-year Jamaican; later Jamaican + Martinique) with the juice of one lime, orange curaçao, orgeat and a little rock-candy syrup, shaken with shaved/crushed ice and garnished with the spent lime shell and a mint sprig: an 'island and palm tree'.

signature.note: Jamaican-led, often split with aged Martinique rhum. Never just light rum (except the Royal Hawaiian variant).
Juice of one lime; keep one spent half-shell.
Dry curaçao preferred.

canonicalSpecs.name: Mai Tai (1944)
canonicalSpecs.source: Victor Bergeron, Trader Vic's, Oakland, 1944, in Vic's own published account (Trader Vic's Book of Food & Drink lineage; quoted by Berry)
garnish: half of the spent lime shell
canonicalSpecs.note: Shake vigorously with plenty of shaved ice; pour unstrained; the lime shell is the island, the mint the palm tree.

canonicalSpecs.name: Mai Tai (Trader Vic's second formula)
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide, revised (1972); Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)

canonicalSpecs.name: Mai Tai (Smuggler's Cove)
canonicalSpecs.source: Martin Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016); Punch

lines.orig: blended aged rum (Denizen Merchant's Reserve: Jamaican + Martinique grand arôme)

canonicalSpecs.name: Royal Hawaiian Mai Tai (1956 recipe)
canonicalSpecs.source: Royal Hawaiian Hotel, Waikiki (Vic's 1953 Matson menu); 1956 hotel recipe documented by Kevin Crossman, ultimatemaitai.com
canonicalSpecs.note: Historical regional variant: lighter rum, smaller modifiers, still no pineapple or orange juice.

ratios.notes: Vic's template 2 : 1 : 1/2 : 1/2 : 1/4 (rum : lime : curaçao : orgeat : rock candy). Nothing else goes in.

never: paper umbrella as the only garnish

archetypes.look: Double old fashioned packed with crushed ice; a translucent-to-slightly-cloudy amber/honey-gold liquid (aged rum + orgeat haze, never red, never orange-juice orange), the spent lime half-shell floating face-down like an island with a big mint sprig rising beside it as the palm tree. One color top to bottom: no float.
substitutions: Appleton 12 / Hamilton Jamaican Pot Still Gold + Clément VSOP for the 17-year Wray & Nephew
Pierre Ferrand Dry Curaçao or Clément Créole Shrubb for DeKuyper
demerara syrup or 2:1 cane syrup for rock candy syrup
a split of Jamaican + Demerara (Death & Co)
redFlags: hurricane glass with umbrella and fruit salad
served without mint or without the lime shell

archetypes.name: Trader Vic's Mai Tai Template (Honi Honi & kin)
archetypes.definition: Vic's own move: keep the Mai Tai's lime, orange curaçao, orgeat and rock candy exactly, and change only the spirit (bourbon, light rum, tequila).
classics: Menehune Juice (Trader Vic, light rum, early 1970s)
Pinky Gonzales (Trader Vic, tequila, Señor Pico, 1964)

canonicalSpecs.name: Honi Honi
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (rev. 1972)

canonicalSpecs.name: Menehune Juice
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's, early 1970s (ultimatemaitai.com)
canonicalSpecs.note: Proportions follow Vic's Mai Tai mix template; exact menu spec not verified.

canonicalSpecs.name: Pinky Gonzales
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Señor Pico, 1964 (Difford's Guide; ultimatemaitai.com)
canonicalSpecs.note: Original: 1 1/2 oz Trader Vic's Mai Tai Mix + 1 1/2 oz tequila (+ lime). The mix is curaçao + orgeat + rock candy; proportions here are reconstructed.

ratios.notes: Same template as the Mai Tai with a different base spirit.

archetypes.look: As a Mai Tai but paler: honey-gold (bourbon), near-clear pale straw with a soft almond haze (light rum or tequila); crushed ice, lime shell and mint.
substitutions: rye for bourbon
reposado or mezcal split for blanco tequila
agave syrup for rock candy with tequila
redFlags: calling it a Mai Tai without the curaçao-orgeat pair

archetypes.name: Scorpion
archetypes.definition: Trader Vic's orgeat punch: light rum with a smaller measure of brandy (and sometimes gin), lemon and orange juice and orgeat, blended or shaken and served by the bowl for sharing.
classics: Scorpion Bowl (Smuggler's Cove, after The Luau 1958)

signature.note: Per serving.
Per serving.
Vic used lemon.

optional.note: In the 1946 bowl and most modern bowls.
Per serving; the 1946 bowl is a true wine punch.

canonicalSpecs.name: Scorpion (individual)
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide, revised (1972)
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend with a scoop of shaved ice, pour into a grapefruit-supreme glass, add ice cubes.

canonicalSpecs.name: Scorpion Bowl (1946)
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Book of Food and Drink (1946), p. 77
canonicalSpecs.note: Steep two hours, add ice, serve in a bowl.

canonicalSpecs.name: Scorpion Bowl (Smuggler's Cove)
canonicalSpecs.source: Martin Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2010/2016), adapted from The Luau, Beverly Hills, 1958; serves 4
canonicalSpecs.note: Roll between two pitchers with 1 1/2 cups crushed ice; pour into a Scorpion bowl.

canonicalSpecs.name: Scorpion (Kelbo's)
canonicalSpecs.source: Kelbo's, Los Angeles (Hank Riddle), 1950s; Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)

ratios.notes: Per serving. Orange juice (1-2 oz) is not counted in sourOz but adds most of the volume. Bowls scale linearly; serve 2-4 from a 32-64 oz bowl.

typical: flaming lime shell / 151 in the volcano well (bowl, theatrical)

archetypes.look: A cloudy pale orange-straw liquid (orange juice + orgeat make it opaque and creamy-looking, lemon keeps it pale) over crushed ice; in the bowl, a wide ceramic vessel with several long straws and a floating gardenia, sometimes a small flaming well in the center. No layers.
substitutions: pisco or Cognac for California brandy
lime for lemon (SC)
a dash of demerara syrup if the orange is tart

archetypes.name: Fog Cutter
archetypes.definition: A tall orgeat punch of rum, brandy and gin with lemon and orange, finished with a float of sherry.

signature.note: Floated, not shaken in. Vic's Samoan version specifies cream sherry (oloroso + PX); Smuggler's Cove uses oloroso. The vocabulary lacks both (see missingIngredients).

canonicalSpecs.name: Fog Cutter
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Book of Food and Drink (1946) / Bartender's Guide (1947)
canonicalSpecs.note: Shake, pour into a 14 oz glass with ice, float sherry. 'Fog Cutter, hell. After two of these you won't even see the stuff.'

canonicalSpecs.name: Samoan Fog Cutter
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic, 1950s; Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed / Total Tiki
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend 5 seconds with a cup of crushed ice, pour into the Samoan Fog Cutter mug, float the sherry.

canonicalSpecs.name: Fog Cutter (Smuggler's Cove)
canonicalSpecs.source: Martin Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016)

ratios.notes: Vic's Fog Cutter is famously tart (model ~3.5-5:1 with 2 oz lemon vs 1/2 oz orgeat); a generator may push toward 6-8:1 with a touch more orgeat. The sherry float is counted in totalOz.

archetypes.look: Tall and pale: a cloudy straw-to-light-orange body (lemon + orange + orgeat) over crushed ice, capped by a thin darker amber-to-mahogany band of sherry floating on top, which bleeds downward in wisps. Usually in the tall Samoan Fog Cutter mug, so the sherry cap is what shows.
substitutions: pisco for brandy (SC)
oloroso or amontillado for cream sherry (drier)
a 1:1 amontillado + PX blend to imitate cream sherry

archetypes.name: Tortuga
archetypes.definition: Trader Vic's overproof heavyweight: equal measures of overproof Demerara and overproof Cuban/white rum softened by sweet vermouth, with curaçao, crème de cacao, grenadine and three citrus juices, served tall in a chimney glass.
classics: Tortuga (Trader Vic's Book of Food & Drink 1946 / Bartender's Guide 1947)

signature.note: 1 oz each.
1/2 oz each.

canonicalSpecs.name: Tortuga
canonicalSpecs.source: Trader Vic's Book of Food and Drink (1946) / Bartender's Guide (1947, unchanged 1972); via Cocktail Virgin Slut / Vintage American Cocktails

canonicalSpecs.name: Tortuga (modern reading)
canonicalSpecs.source: Modern bar reading (Hamilton 151, Don Q 151, Cocchi di Torino), widely reproduced

ratios.notes: Two overproof rums; sweet vermouth (1 oz) is a modifier and not counted as sweet.

archetypes.look: A deep reddish-amber to mahogany (vermouth + 151 Demerara + a little grenadine) over crushed ice in a chimney glass; translucent with a citrus haze.
substitutions: Don Q 151 or Wray & Nephew Overproof for Havana Club 123
Hamilton 151 for Lemon Hart 151
redFlags: confusing it with the agricole + ginger beer Tortuga

archetypes.name: Passion Sour (Saturn & Port Light)
archetypes.definition: A golden-era tiki sour built on a non-rum spirit (gin or bourbon) with lemon and passion fruit syrup, rounded by orgeat and falernum (Saturn) or honey and grenadine (Port Light).

canonicalSpecs.name: Saturn
canonicalSpecs.source: J. 'Popo' Galsini (Kona Kai; California Bartenders' Guild winner, 1967); Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
garnish: lemon peel ring around a cherry (the planet and its rings)
canonicalSpecs.note: Blend with crushed ice; often served in a coupe or pilsner today.

canonicalSpecs.name: Port Light (Kahiki)
canonicalSpecs.source: Kahiki Supper Club, Columbus, c. 1961 (as presented by Mixing Up Tiki)

canonicalSpecs.name: Port Light (Smuggler's Cove)
canonicalSpecs.source: Martin Cate, Smuggler's Cove (2016)

ratios.notes: Saturn sits sweet-tart at ~14:1 (blended); Port Light at 6-11:1.

archetypes.look: Saturn: opaque, frothy pale yellow-gold (passion fruit), creamy from blending, a curl of lemon peel ringing a red cherry. Port Light (Kahiki): a translucent rosy amber-red (grenadine + bourbon) - the red port-side running light; Smuggler's version is a foamy golden-peach with a white egg-white cap.
substitutions: passion fruit purée + simple syrup for passion fruit syrup
rye for bourbon
Old Tom for London dry
redFlags: passion fruit liqueur instead of syrup making it cloying

archetypes.name: Bitter Tiki (Jungle Bird & Bitter Mai Tai)
archetypes.definition: A tropical sour in which Campari (or another red bitter) is a major component, paired with dark/funky rum and either pineapple (Jungle Bird line) or the Mai Tai's orgeat and curaçao (Bitter Mai Tai line), with lime.
classics: Jungle Bird (Jeffrey Ong, Kuala Lumpur Hilton, 1973)
Bitter Mai Tai (Jeremy Oertel, Dram, Brooklyn, c. 2012)

signature.note: An ounce-level measure, not a dash.
Jungle Bird: 1 1/2 (modern) to 4 oz (1973) pineapple + 1/2 oz demerara/simple. Bitter Mai Tai: 3/4 orgeat + 1/2 curaçao.

canonicalSpecs.name: Jungle Bird (1973)
canonicalSpecs.source: Jeffrey Ong, Aviary Bar, Kuala Lumpur Hilton, 1973; via John J. Poister (1989) and Jeff Berry, Intoxica! (2002)
canonicalSpecs.note: Originally served in a bird-shaped ceramic vessel.

canonicalSpecs.name: Jungle Bird (González)
canonicalSpecs.source: Giuseppe González re-spec, New York, c. 2010 (widely reproduced)

canonicalSpecs.name: Bitter Mai Tai
canonicalSpecs.source: Jeremy Oertel, Dram (Brooklyn), c. 2012; Punch / Easy Tiki (2021)

ratios.notes: baseOz counts rum only; Campari (0.75-1.5 oz) is counted in sweetOz. Bitterness lets these carry a higher sugar:acid than a Don sour without tasting sweet.

archetypes.look: Jungle Bird: an opaque coral/salmon-red with a fine pineapple froth on top (Campari's red diluted into yellow pineapple), darker brick-red in the modern short version. Bitter Mai Tai: vivid translucent red-orange to scarlet over crushed ice with a mint sprig. Never brown, never pink-pastel.
substitutions: Cynar or Aperol for Campari (lighter / earthier)
Coruba or Goslings for blackstrap rum
Hamilton Pot Still Black for Smith & Cross
redFlags: Campari in dashes (then it is not a bitter tiki drink)
stack of Don spices on top of the bitter

archetypes.name: Bitters-as-Base Sour (Trinidad Sour)
archetypes.definition: An inversion in which Angostura bitters (an ounce or more) is the base, softened by an equal-ish measure of orgeat and given acid by lemon or lime, with a small spirit backbone.

signature.note: The orgeat fat tames the bitters; do not swap for plain syrup.

canonicalSpecs.name: Trinidad Sour
canonicalSpecs.source: Giuseppe González, Clover Club (Brooklyn), 2009; Punch / Difford's
canonicalSpecs.note: Shake hard with ice; strain into a chilled coupe.

canonicalSpecs.name: Trinidad Especial
canonicalSpecs.source: Valentino Bolognese, 2008 competition drink (Kindred Cocktails / Difford's)

ratios.notes: Angostura (44.7% ABV) is the true base: 1-1.5 oz of it supplies most of the alcohol even though baseOz shows only the small rye/pisco pour.

archetypes.look: Served up in a coupe: an opaque brick-red to garnet-brown liquid with a pinkish-tan micro-foam from the shaken orgeat; looks like a dark rosé gone to rust.
substitutions: pisco for rye (Especial)
lime for lemon
redFlags: Angostura in dashes (then it is a normal sour)
served tall over ice with fruit

archetypes.name: Tropical Old Fashioned / Negroni
archetypes.definition: A spirit-forward stirred drink in Old Fashioned or Negroni form where a characterful rum carries the base and a tropical/tiki modifier (falernum, allspice, li hing mui, Campari) is measured in barspoons to ounces, with no juice.

signature.note: Barspoon of syrup for the Old Fashioned; ounce-level vermouth + bitter for the Negroni.

canonicalSpecs.name: Kingston Negroni
canonicalSpecs.source: Joaquín Simó, Death & Co, 2009 (menu spring 2010); Punch

canonicalSpecs.name: Paniolo Old Fashioned
canonicalSpecs.source: Repo record attributes it to Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 203; NOT verified by search this session

ratios.notes: No citrus, so sugar:acid does not apply (null). Old Fashioned form: 2 oz rum + 1 barspoon-1 tsp syrup + bitters; Negroni form: 1:1:1 rum, Campari, sweet vermouth (Campari counted as sweet).

archetypes.look: Clear and glossy over a single large cube: deep amber (Old Fashioned) or translucent garnet-red (Kingston Negroni), with an expressed orange peel.
substitutions: Hamilton Pot Still Gold for Smith & Cross
falernum or allspice dram barspoon for li hing mui
